throughput.mib_per_s_status: HISTORICAL. The original phase-3 benchmark script's figure: no box, no date, no commit, and -- the part that matters -- NO STATED WINDOW, so it cannot be compared with sustained_mib_per_s below, which is timed from the first byte on disk to the last. Kept as the record it is. Nothing derives a ceiling from it any more (plan §18 item 61), for the same reason idle_cost.total_cpu_percent stopped being one at item 46: a number with no provenance cannot be re-measured, and a ceiling nobody can reproduce is a ceiling nobody can defend. The 30 MiB/s headroom_target beside it is unchanged and is still the recorded exit criterion.
throughput.headroom_basis: 10x over 8 ports at 3 Mbaud (3 MB/s aggregate)

provenance.what: sustained_mib_per_s is the LOW end of the healthy unloaded readings on the box below, timed from the first byte in the log sink to the last -- the daemon's own window, excluding the sim double's payload generation (1.08-1.10 s for 256 MiB in an unoptimised build, which completes before the first byte moves). reference_ratio_ceiling is what itest/tests/p3_firehose.rs actually asserts: the ratio of what a null consumer moves through the same pty double, on the same box, in the same run, to what the daemon moves. See that file's header for the derivation.
provenance.box: 20-core x86_64, Linux 7.0.0-29-generic, run dir on tmpfs, debug (unoptimised workspace) build
provenance.commit: 7410b62, in a detached worktree; the shared tree carried unrelated concurrent edits and was deliberately not used for the controls
provenance.saturated_load: 20 spinning shell loops on 20 cores, load average 7.5-32.3 across the samples -- a deliberately pathological arm, harsher than the default `cargo test --workspace` gate, and the reason no absolute wall-clock floor is asserted per run
provenance.source_is_the_ceiling: The sim double drained by a bare read loop with NO DAEMON delivers 256 MiB at 440-535 MiB/s here, against the daemon's 460-558 MiB/s on the same box. The daemon is not the bottleneck on this path: it keeps pace with a null consumer to within 15 %. This is what the ratio measures, and it is why the confound plan §18 item 61 named first (the source's own rate) became the instrument rather than a term to subtract.
provenance.why_no_absolute_floor: Load moves the wall-clock reading by 30x on one box and one tree (the two healthy arrays above). Asserting the recorded 30 MiB/s exit criterion per run would have reddened a HEALTHY tree in five of the twelve saturated runs, and notes §3.69 records the same guard reading ~4 MB/s on an 8-core box under a load of 19.6 with nothing wrong. The criterion is therefore enforced against the recorded FIGURES, in p3_firehose::criterion, and never against the box running the test. The 60 s deadline (a 4.27 MiB/s stall detector) is unchanged, so nothing shipped got looser. Daemon CPU per MiB was evaluated as a load-independent alternative and rejected on measurement: it moves 7x with load (2.78-3.63 unloaded against 9.6-22.2 saturated), which is better than 30x and still too wide to carry a ceiling. It is printed, not asserted.
provenance.controls: Five regression classes planted in a detached worktree at 7410b62, each built and run against this file's own guard. Every one of them either leaves the ratio under 3 or arrives as a STALL that the 60 s deadline catches; not one lands in the band a tightened throughput floor would cover. The pipeline is bistable -- it keeps pace with a null consumer to within ~3x, or it collapses below 4.3 MiB/s -- and nothing measured sits between 4.3 and 108 MiB/s.
provenance.control_ring_vecdeque: The defect §5 clause 3 names: ReplayRing's fixed circular Vec<u8> replaced by a VecDeque<u8> drain+extend. STALLS at 13-43 % of the stream and sits there (37108667 B and 116432277 B in two runs, 37402492 B in a third on the shared tree, where the daemon then reported `usb0 waiting (device lost: read returned EOF)` -- the blocked source took an EIO). The functional suite does not see it: the plant is correct, only slow. 3 runs, all FAILED at the deadline.
provenance.control_ring_per_byte: The same fixed circular Vec, written one byte at a time (the mildest per-byte form there is). 43518252, 47396986 and 47416214 B in 60 s = 0.69-0.75 MiB/s. 3 runs, all FAILED at the deadline.
provenance.control_mirror_cost: A calibrated spin, and a calibrated sleep, on the mirror path per chunk. 4 us: 390 MiB/s (no effect). 10 us: 493. 20 us: 382. 24 us: 4.25 (collapsed, 99.7 % delivered at the deadline). 26 us: 3.53. 28 us: 3.15. 30 us: 3.94. 50 us: 2.41. 100 us (sleep): 1.17. 200 us (sleep): 0.49. 2 ms: 0.083. The cliff between 20 and 24 us is a 90x change in throughput for a 1.2x change in the injected cost.
provenance.control_read_buf: runtime::READ_BUF, the documented `fewer, larger reads per idle gap` constant (§15.18), shrunk from 64 KiB. 4096: 466.7 MiB/s, ratio 0.97. 1024: 200.9 MiB/s, ratio 1.75, 10.602 ms CPU/MiB. 512: 137.6 and 135.6 MiB/s, ratio 2.92 and 0.85, 17.0-17.9 ms CPU/MiB. 320: 107.8 MiB/s ratio 2.75 on one run and a stall at 99.8 % on another -- the same value, both branches. 384 and 256: stalls at 99.8 %. 128 and 64: reach 99.95 % and hang for the whole 180 s of a deliberately raised deadline. A real constant, a plausible edit, and CPU per MiB tracks it monotonically (4.0 -> 10.6 -> 17.0 -> 23.1) where wall throughput does not.
provenance.refutes: plan §18 item 61's evidence that the ring-storage tripwire is orphaned: 'a VecDeque<u8> drain+extend rewrite would clear 4.27 MiB/s comfortably'. It does not clear it, on either of the two plants that spell it, in six runs. The tripwire was never orphaned. Item 61's other claims stand: the axis printed no reading, and the recorded figure had no provenance.
provenance.ceiling_has_no_code_plant: No code plant reddens the reference_ratio_ceiling. It is proven live and non-vacuous by planting the CRITERION instead -- 8.0 -> 0.5 in this file reddens a healthy run with the guard's full message -- so its passing output is not its not-running output (AGENTS §3). It ships as a backstop against a regression that is slow WITHOUT stalling, and must be quoted as that and not as a guard with fail-first proof behind it (AGENTS §9).

idle_cost.total_cpu_percent_status: HISTORICAL. A single total at 32 idle fds from the original phase-3 benchmark script: no box, no date, no commit, and no baseline rung, so it cannot be decomposed into the daemon's fixed cost and the per-fd cost the poll backoff actually controls. Kept as the record it is. It is no longer the derivation for the drift tripwire, because an absolute total is dominated by the fixed term: on the 20-core box below the fixed term alone is 1.194 %, so 1.75x of this 2.00 % put the ceiling at 3.50 % where the healthy reading is 3.3-3.6 % and the guard fired with the mechanism measurably intact (plan §18 item 46). The 20 % budget_percent beside it is unchanged and is still the recorded exit criterion.
idle_cost.mechanism: adaptive poll backoff to IDLE_POLL when quiescent (§15.18/§15.19)

per_fd_provenance.what: per_fd_cpu_percent is the marginal cost of one additional idle tty fd, in percent of one core. It is the quantity design §15.19 records (~0.06 %/fd) and the quantity the ACTIVE_POLL->IDLE_POLL backoff controls; the fixed cost of a running daemon is a different term and belongs to the box.
per_fd_provenance.box: 20-core x86_64, Linux 7.0.0-29-generic, load between 1.0 and 2.5 at every sample
per_fd_provenance.control: the same sweep with daemon/src/runtime.rs's `back_off` body replaced by `let _ = wait;` and the workspace rebuilt, so every idle fd re-polls at ACTIVE_POLL forever
per_fd_provenance.separation: 2.75x in the slope (0.2004 / 0.0728). The healthy slope reproduces design §15.19's ~0.06 %/fd within 20 %, so the backoff has not regressed: that is the disposition plan §18 item 46 asked for, decided by measurement and REFUTING the 'the backoff regressed' branch of the guard's own failure message.
per_fd_provenance.guard_form: itest/tests/p3_idle_cost.rs measures the two-rung difference (baseline_tty_fds -> idle_tty_fds) inside one daemon process, which cancels the fixed term by construction. On the healthy data above that form reads (3.467 - 1.800) / 24 = 0.069 %/fd, 5 % under the 15-point fit; on the control data it reads (9.850 - 5.000) / 24 = 0.202 %/fd.
